risk_heading: Product Performance and Defect Risks for Our Industrial Components
paragraph_text:
We manufacture industrial components used in critical applications, including equipment that operates under high load, temperature, and vibration. If defects occur due to material inconsistencies, calibration errors, machining tolerances, or supplier variations, the components could fail prematurely or perform below required specifications. Because our products are typically integrated into end-user systems, identifying and containing failures may be difficult and can result in significant downtime for customers.

When performance issues arise, customers may request replacements, impose warranty claims, or seek damages for consequential losses. We may also face product liability litigation if a defect contributes to property damage or personal injury. Even if we ultimately prevail, defending claims can be time-consuming and costly. Moreover, any corrective action—such as engineering changes, additional inspections, or enhanced quality controls—may increase operating expenses and affect delivery schedules.

If we are required to issue notices, revise specifications, or conduct broad replacement programs, our reputation and customer relationships could be harmed, and our results of operations could be adversely affected.

risk_heading: Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities in Our Connected Consumer Applications
paragraph_text:
A portion of our offerings is delivered through connected applications that collect and process user-generated information to provide features such as personalization, usage analytics, and remote control. These applications may contain security vulnerabilities that could be exploited by unauthorized parties to access or manipulate user data, compromise device behavior, or disrupt service. While we implement encryption, authentication controls, and monitoring, threats evolve and may not be detected in time to prevent harm.

If we experience a security incident involving our products, we could face contractual claims from customers, consumer protection complaints, and potential product-related liability if compromised systems cause physical harm or unsafe operating conditions. For example, unauthorized changes to device settings, failed safety interlocks, or incorrect alert messages could lead to accidents. Regulators may also require notifications to affected users and could impose fines or require remediation plans.

In addition to financial losses and increased security and legal costs, any incident could damage our brand and reduce customer willingness to adopt our products. If vulnerabilities are discovered by third parties or regulators before we have implemented mitigations, the resulting public attention and litigation could materially affect our business.

risk_heading: Risks of Inaccurate Labeling and Chemical Safety Compliance
paragraph_text:
We distribute consumer and industrial products that include regulated chemical ingredients and require accurate labeling regarding hazards, concentration, and intended use. If labels, safety data sheets, or packaging are incorrect—whether due to changes in formulations, translation errors, or inventory mix-ups—we could face regulatory enforcement, product seizures, and consumer claims. Mislabeling may also cause end-users to handle products improperly, increasing the likelihood of injuries or property damage.

Although we seek to maintain robust document control and supplier oversight, ingredient sourcing can change and formulations can be updated as we improve performance or respond to customer requirements. Any failure to implement changes correctly across manufacturing, warehousing, and distribution channels could result in release of nonconforming product. In addition, certain jurisdictions impose specific requirements for packaging, child-resistant features, and disposal instructions.

If we are found to have failed to comply with applicable chemical and consumer product safety regulations, we may be required to recall products, fund remediation, and incur significant legal costs. Product liability lawsuits could allege that exposures caused illness or other harm. Our insurance may not cover all claims, and defense costs could adversely affect our operating results.

risk_heading: Warranty and Indemnification Obligations for Our Software-as-a-Service
paragraph_text:
We provide subscription-based services that integrate with customers’ systems to deliver workflow automation and reporting. While the services are intended to function as described in our documentation, they may contain errors, defects, or configuration issues that lead to incorrect outputs. These errors can affect downstream decisions, such as inventory ordering, billing, risk scoring, and compliance reporting. If our customers rely on incorrect information, they could incur losses and assert claims for breach of contract, indemnification, or damages.

In certain agreements, we may provide limited warranties and indemnify customers for specific categories of claims. If those commitments do not fully cover a dispute, we could bear costs directly. Additionally, if an error is alleged to have caused harm to customers’ end-users, regulators may investigate whether our service requirements, disclosures, and quality processes were adequate.

Although we conduct testing and monitor service health, failures may occur due to changes in external systems, unusual customer data, or scaling issues. Detecting defects can also be challenging when failures appear only under particular usage patterns. A significant dispute or an expanding indemnification obligation could materially increase costs and divert management attention.

risk_heading: Risks Associated With Data Privacy Failures Connected to Our Platforms
paragraph_text:
We collect information from customers and end-users to operate our platforms and to support product functionality, such as identity verification, account access, and customer communications. Despite privacy-by-design practices, security controls, and contractual safeguards with vendors, we may be unable to prevent all privacy violations or unauthorized access. A failure could occur due to software defects, misconfiguration, employee error, or third-party breaches.

If our products do not protect personal information as intended, we could face regulatory enforcement and litigation. Claims may allege that we exposed end-users to identity theft, fraud, or other harms and that we failed to meet consumer protection requirements. In some jurisdictions, failure to safeguard data can be treated as a wrongful act tied to product and service delivery, exposing us to damages, settlements, and reputational harm.

Furthermore, certain customers require us to meet specific security and privacy standards as a condition of contracting. If we cannot satisfy those requirements after changes to our products or to applicable laws, customers may terminate agreements or demand remediation. Such disputes may also require us to provide additional credits, refunds, or indemnities.

Although we maintain insurance and invest in security programs, the costs associated with a significant privacy incident—including legal expenses, remediation, and notification—could be material.

risk_heading: Product Liability Exposure From Alleged Defects in Therapeutic Formulations
paragraph_text:
We develop and manufacture therapeutic formulations for prescription and non-prescription use. If our manufacturing process fails to consistently produce product within required specifications, or if impurities are present at unacceptable levels, the resulting batches could be ineffective or potentially harmful to patients. Even with quality controls and batch release testing, undetected deviations may occur and could lead to adverse medical events.

If evidence emerges that a product defect contributed to injuries or illnesses, healthcare providers or patients may pursue claims for damages, and regulators may initiate investigations. In addition, we could be required to conduct recall campaigns, discontinue affected lots, or implement risk-management plans. Recalls can also impair our ability to supply customers and may create demand for alternative products, which could lead to lost revenue.

Regulatory scrutiny can extend beyond the affected product to our broader quality system. If regulators determine that our procedures or documentation are inadequate, we could incur remediation costs and face restrictions on future manufacturing approvals. Our insurance may not fully cover the costs of litigation, adverse-event analysis, or settlements.

A significant product-related adverse event, recall, or litigation could materially affect our business, financial condition, and operating results.

risk_heading: Risks From Reliance on Third-Party Manufacturing and Components
paragraph_text:
We outsource portions of manufacturing, assembly, and logistics for certain products and depend on third parties to meet quality, safety, and regulatory requirements. If a supplier uses substandard materials, fails to follow agreed specifications, or does not implement adequate process controls, defects may be introduced into products distributed to customers. In addition, third parties may experience disruptions or workforce constraints that affect production consistency.

Because outsourced components may be integrated into complex systems, identifying a defect as originating from a specific supplier can take time. During that period, defective products may be shipped and installed, increasing the likelihood of warranty claims, returns, and recall actions. We may also become subject to legal claims asserting that we failed to maintain adequate oversight.

We maintain supplier qualification programs and audit rights; however, these measures may not prevent all compliance failures or quality issues. A significant supplier-related product incident could result in expensive remediation, loss of customers, and potential liability for personal injury or property damage.

Moreover, any corrective actions required by regulators may lead to higher costs and delays in meeting demand. These factors could adversely affect our operating results and financial condition.

risk_heading: Liability Risk Related to Our Safety-Critical Navigation and Control Systems
paragraph_text:
Some of our products provide navigation and automated control functions that may be used in safety-critical environments. If our software logic contains defects, if sensors provide inaccurate readings, or if data inputs are corrupted, the system may make incorrect decisions. In safety-critical contexts, even a limited defect can lead to significant operational harm, including accidents and injuries.

We seek to mitigate these risks through design verification testing, redundancy, and validation procedures; however, no testing program can guarantee performance in all conditions. Real-world environments can vary in ways that are difficult to replicate in laboratory settings, including abnormal weather, electromagnetic interference, or sensor calibration drift. Additionally, updates to operating systems or integration with customer platforms can affect performance.

If our products contribute to an incident, we may be subject to regulatory actions, indemnification obligations, and lawsuits brought by customers, passengers, or other third parties. Plaintiffs may allege that we failed to warn users adequately or that our software updates were not sufficiently robust. Defense costs and settlement obligations could be material, and adverse publicity could reduce demand.

To the extent we are required to issue software patches, replace components, or conduct field retrofit programs, our costs may increase and our product roadmap could be delayed.

Because vehicle safety is heavily regulated and monitored, even a quality issue affecting a small segment of production can trigger broad customer actions, including warranty claims, stoppage of shipments, and recalls.

Any material recall, warranty expense, or litigation could adversely affect our margins, cash flows, and ability to compete in the parts market.

If a part does not meet design specifications or is produced with material defects, it may wear prematurely, function improperly, or fail under stress. Because vehicle safety is heavily regulated and monitored, even a quality issue affecting a small segment of production can trigger broad customer actions, including warranty claims, stoppage of shipments, and recalls.

Our customers may require us to accept returns, reimburse labor costs, and provide indemnification for alleged failures connected to our parts. In addition, vehicle owners may assert product liability claims if the part contributes to collisions or injuries. Although we conduct inspections and quality checks, defects can escape detection due to complex manufacturing steps, variability in inspection standards among facilities, or changes in supplier processes.

Defending claims and working with regulators to address nonconformities may require substantial resources and could delay delivery of replacement parts. If we are unable to achieve timely corrective actions, customers may reduce orders or transition to alternative suppliers.

Any material recall, warranty expense, or litigation could adversely affect our margins, cash flows, and ability to compete in the parts market.

risk_heading: Risks Related to Packaging Materials and Downstream Safety Incidents
paragraph_text:
We use packaging materials for food, personal care, and other consumer products. Packaging must meet safety standards and function as intended to protect products during storage and transportation. If packaging is contaminated, fails to provide an effective barrier, or is made with materials that do not comply with regulatory requirements, the packaged goods may become unsafe or degrade in ways that create health risks.

In some cases, suppliers of packaging components can change material sources or manufacturing processes without sufficient notice, which may impact compatibility with our product formulations. Also, distribution conditions such as humidity, heat, or physical impact can cause packaging deterioration. Even if the main product is within specification, compromised packaging could lead to leaks, incorrect labeling, or cross-contamination.

If an incident occurs, we may be required to recall affected lots and incur costs related to customer notifications, refunds, and destruction of inventory. In addition, we may face allegations that we failed to provide adequate warnings or that our packaging design did not anticipate realistic distribution risks.

We maintain quality and regulatory compliance programs; however, such measures may not prevent all failures. Material product claims and recall expenses could negatively impact our financial results and operating cash flows.

risk_heading: Regulatory and Litigation Exposure From Misuse of Our Nutritional Supplements
paragraph_text:
We market nutritional supplements that are intended to be used according to labeling and dosage instructions. Adverse events can occur if products are improperly manufactured, if dosages are inaccurate, or if products contain contaminants. Even when our testing demonstrates compliance at the time of release, results may vary across batches or due to storage conditions before consumption.

If consumers experience side effects, regulators may request documentation regarding manufacturing records, ingredient sourcing, and quality testing. Regulators may also impose additional testing or require corrective actions. Claims by consumers or healthcare providers could allege that we sold defective products or failed to warn about potential risks associated with specific ingredients.

We work with ingredient suppliers and perform batch-level testing; however, limitations in testing sensitivity, changes in supplier processes, or unexpected contamination events could lead to nonconforming product. In addition, for certain supplements, we must rely on third-party analytical testing, and delays or disputes regarding test results may complicate our response.

A recall or significant litigation could result in substantial costs, including refunds, inventory write-offs, legal fees, and increased regulatory compliance expenditures. These matters could also harm our brand and reduce demand.

risk_heading: Cyber Incident Remediation Costs and Product-Related Claims in Our Cloud Services
paragraph_text:
We operate cloud services that are used to store and transmit customer content. A cybersecurity incident affecting our cloud environment could result in loss, alteration, or exposure of customer data. Although we deploy security tooling, vulnerability management, and incident response processes, there can be no assurance that our controls will prevent unauthorized access or disruption.

If an incident occurs, we may be obligated to notify affected parties and regulators, and to provide remediation and support. Customers may assert that outages or data compromise constitute a failure to deliver contracted services and could seek credits, service termination, or damages. In some cases, customers may claim that our product controls were insufficient and that the incident led to downstream harms such as fraud, business interruption, or consumer injury.

We may also face investigations or enforcement actions related to the security and availability of our offerings. Even unsuccessful attacks can cause operational interruptions and increased costs to restore service and strengthen defenses.

Because incident response efforts may require significant personnel time, legal resources, and third-party expertise, remediation costs could be material. A severe incident could adversely affect our ability to retain existing customers and attract new customers.

risk_heading: Liability From Nonconforming Food-Contact Materials and Contamination Risks
paragraph_text:
We use components that come into contact with food and beverages. These food-contact materials must comply with applicable safety standards and must maintain proper integrity throughout the product’s lifecycle, including manufacturing, storage, and distribution. Contamination may occur if materials are produced in environments with cross-contact, if they are improperly cleaned, or if protective coatings degrade faster than expected.

If a contamination event is discovered by customers or regulators, we could be required to recall products, halt shipments, or replace inventory. Even if only certain batches are affected, the scope of customer actions could be broader due to consumer safety concerns and uncertainty about where contamination may exist. Claims could be brought by customers for breach of contract, indemnification, or negligence, and by consumers if they experience adverse health effects.

We maintain quality testing and supplier oversight; however, contaminants may be intermittent and may not be detected until after distribution. In addition, regulatory expectations can change over time, which may require us to update testing methods, labeling, and product specifications.

Significant contamination claims, recalls, or governmental enforcement could materially adversely affect our revenue, margins, and reputation.

risk_heading: Potential Exposure for Alleged Inadequate Warnings or Instructions
paragraph_text:
Our products are accompanied by instructions, safety warnings, and, where applicable, prescribing information intended to guide use. If users misunderstand instructions, if warnings are insufficiently clear, or if new information about product risks emerges after distribution, we could face claims that we failed to provide adequate warnings. The risk is heightened when products have multiple operating modes, involve maintenance by third parties, or are used in environments that differ from those described in documentation.

We periodically review product labeling and updates; however, regulatory or scientific developments can occur that require rapid changes. Delays in implementing updated instructions—such as changes to printed materials or distribution of revised digital documentation—could leave earlier versions in circulation. In addition, we may rely on distributors and service partners to transmit updated guidance to end-users.

If a product incident occurs, plaintiffs may argue that a failure to warn or instruct was a contributing factor to injuries or losses. Regulatory agencies may also pursue enforcement actions if labeling is found misleading or incomplete. Defense costs and settlements could be substantial, particularly where claims involve personal injuries or large numbers of affected users.

To the extent we must conduct warning campaigns, issue corrected materials, or retrofit equipment, associated costs could adversely impact our financial results.

risk_heading: Risks of Liability Due to Component Authentication and Anti-Tampering Failures
paragraph_text:
Certain products include authentication features and anti-tampering mechanisms designed to confirm product authenticity and prevent unsafe modifications. If these controls can be bypassed, if cryptographic keys are compromised, or if the authentication workflow is improperly implemented, unauthorized users could alter product behavior or use counterfeit components. Such conduct can create safety hazards for customers and disrupt our ability to ensure product integrity.

We rely on secure design practices and third-party components to implement these mechanisms, but vulnerabilities may be discovered over time or introduced through software updates and integrations. If an attacker successfully defeats authentication, we could face increased returns, warranty costs, and disputes with customers and distributors.

In addition, if tampering leads to an incident—such as incorrect dosing, miscalibrated operation, or unsafe system states—we may be exposed to product liability claims and regulatory scrutiny. Plaintiffs may assert that we did not adequately protect our products or that our monitoring and response were insufficient.

We also may incur expenses related to field monitoring, remediation, and replacement of affected units. Any significant security or tampering-related event could materially affect our reputation and financial performance.

risk_heading: Environmental-Health Claims Tied to Our Product Use and Disposal Instructions
paragraph_text:
Although we focus on product safety and compliance throughout the life of our offerings, customers’ use and disposal practices can affect potential exposure risks. If product instructions, disposal guidance, or warnings regarding safe handling are incomplete or become outdated, end-users may improperly store, discard, or reuse products. This can lead to health and safety issues and may also result in claims that our products were defective or that we failed to provide adequate guidance.

We seek to provide instructions consistent with regulatory requirements; however, state and local rules regarding disposal may differ and change. Additionally, some customers may distribute products through independent channels, which can lead to inconsistent labeling or delayed dissemination of revised materials.

If a health or safety incident occurs, regulators may investigate not only the incident circumstances but also our compliance with disclosure obligations and our design and quality processes. We could face enforcement actions, civil litigation, and settlements. Even where incidents are attributable to misuse, plaintiffs may argue that our products were unreasonably dangerous due to inadequate warnings.

Remediation efforts could include product take-backs, replacements, and updates to labeling and training materials for distributors. Such obligations could be costly and could adversely affect our financial results.

risk_heading: Potential Liability for Defects in Our Consumer Home Appliances
paragraph_text:
Our home appliances are designed to operate safely and efficiently for extended periods. Defects in motors, heating elements, wiring, control boards, or safety switches may cause overheating, electrical faults, or failure of protective mechanisms. In addition, manufacturing variances can result in inconsistent assembly, which may affect safe operation. While we conduct quality checks, failures may occur due to component tolerances, supplier changes, or errors that appear only after prolonged use.

If customers experience malfunctions, we may be obligated to provide repairs, replace units under warranty, or participate in recall programs. We could also face product liability claims related to property damage, injuries, or alleged failure to meet consumer safety standards. If an incident receives media attention, it could lead to increased returns and reduced demand.

Regulatory authorities may require corrective actions if products are found to be noncompliant with electrical safety requirements or if safety testing reveals potential hazards. Even if we ultimately determine there is no defect, responding to investigations and litigation could be costly and time-consuming.

A major safety event could adversely affect our reputation, increase costs, and materially impact our results of operations.
